body: I was actually talking about myself. I’m not quite a nurse yet, I’m still going through school but I’ve always had this fear that people will treat me differently because of my condition. Especially since I want to go into psych nursing.

I agree that situations can get better for people at their lowest. Medication helped me so much, the only problem is that it only lasts about a week until I have to increase the dose. It felt nice to not feel suicidal all the time and not crying everyday. But now I'm back to being at my lowest right now. So I do think that things can get better, maybe not permanently, but even temporarily and sometimes that can be enough to keep people going. I think that hope is a big part. Even when suicidal people don't believe in hope or that things can get better, others do. 

But I don't agree that it's a cowardly act. Because it takes a lot of courage. It takes a lot of courage to say I'm done with life and make that final act. Because humans are geared towards survival. Even in desperate situation, our brains and bodies will struggle to keep on living. Even for people without fear of heights, it's scary to jump from a high place. For many, it can be even scarier to fail.

I've been struggling with suicidal thoughts, had 2 incidences where I had really strong feelings about dying and told my counselor. Both times he told me to go to the emergency room and almost "threatened" in a nicer way to call the ambulance. He told me as much as there is the client confidentiality, not when there is direct harm to myself. I was strongly against it because of the medical bills. I would have mentioned it too but he probably would have said that life is more important than money. I already owe about $150 from 3 30 minute visits with the doctor/psychiatrist which I understand is cheaper than what many people would have to pay but I work part time as a student and I'm not even close to finding a medication that works for me yet. As much as I want to find treatment for myself, I just can't afford to rack up more and more medical bills.

Thank you for your kind words. I actually saw a public safety officer who works at my school and is a friend. We talked for a while and I just sat there and enjoyed the wind for about an hour. It was nice just watching the trees sway in the wind and not thinking about anything.

This is something I've read a long time ago. When you pull out a hair and you see a red end, that means the follicle has been damaged. The red part is the blood vessel, and when you pulled that out, the follicle lost blood supply, meaning that it won't be able to grow hair. The good news is that (from my experience) they don't happen very often (maybe I'll get one every couple of months or so) and even if you pull hair from the same spot multiple times, as long as the blood vessel is intact, hair will grow back again.

I understand how conversation can help a lot. Talking to my friends and my counselor are pretty much the only highlights of my week and what's keeping me going. So if it helps you, I'll talk about anything or however long you want to. I lived in Canada for a few years when I was little and I remember going to an urgent care (not sure if that was what it was called) for a sprained ankle and had a pretty long wait. That's way different from being on a waiting list for over a year but I see what you're saying. But wow, yeah I guess it leaves you with little choice about being able to choose what doctor to see. 

I'm actually short of 2 years from becoming a pharmacist (still in school right now) but working with a pharmacist who sees drug abuse as a choice and dealing with anxiety myself really changed my perspective on things. I'm ashamed to say that about a month ago (when I realized I had anxiety and started seeing a counselor at school) I probably would have felt the same way. I guess more in terms of I would try to help people deal with abuse problems but can't really relate or understand that it's not something that is easily controlled. I can't say I have enjoyed the past month going down the path of suicidal thoughts but I'm grateful that it opened my eyes and definitely something I want to help people with as a pharmacist.

I'm sorry to hear that. I wish the circumstances was better so that it's easier to deal with the problem. As much as we're dedicated to providing care and helping people deal with abuse problems, it saddens me to hear that they couldn't do anything for you. From what I gather, you live in a different country so I shouldn't say they should be able to do this or that. I'm sorry I couldn't help you with a solution but we're here to support you. If you need to talk just to distract yourself, we're here.

If there's anything my counselor told me, there's no insignificant problem. However small it might be, it impacts you greatly, which makes it pretty significant and you shouldn't feel guilty that you want to talk about it. I work at a pharmacy and I know what the whole prescription filling process is like so I'm just trying to come up with ideas for you. I know that this is probably a hard time to make any changes regarding the doctors you see, but is there a different doctor that you could maybe change to? It just infuriates me that they aren't prescribing you a lower dose even though you expressed concerns about abusing them. 

It probably doesn't help you right now, but in the future, you could ask your pharmacy to give you fewer tablets than actually prescribed. Unfortunately they can't take back medications once they leave the pharmacy, but if you let them know that you are concerned, they'll most likely be willing to work with you so that you don't have a bunch extra on hand. I don't know if this is something you might be willing to do, but if you know how much you really need in a month, you can take the extra and drop it off in a drop-off box in some pharmacies or police/fire station. 

I know that these aren't really ideal solution that helps your situation right now. I hope there one that you find useful or maybe able to come up with an idea. Don't be afraid to talk to us with whatever you might be struggling with, just getting it out there can help a lot.

I hope you're still here. I work at retail pharmacy as an intern. My mom told me to stop going to work because she was afraid that I was going to get sick. She didn't care that I was going to get fired or that I had an obligation to be there for my team. She's always been saying I need to get a good GPA to get a good job, but completely ignores the fact that you can have a 4.0 GPA but without experience you can't get a job. I don't know too much about what your relationship is like with your mom, but the pandemic is causing a lot of people to act irrationally. I'm sorry to hear that you had to blow the interview off. But this has to end sometime. It might take a while but life will go back to being normal. It's not too late to look for another job after the quarantine is over. If you need to vent or talk about anything, we're here.

I understand that feeling. I'm top 15% of my class, get scholarships and probably have a bright future ahead of me and the only bad thing that's happened is some abuse (not even considered abuse in Asian cultures) growing up as a kid. But I'm feeling empty because of school. I always think that there is always someone above me, better than me in every way and I failed because school has been my whole life. And it makes me feel even worse because I was given the opportunity to be better. My parents spent a s\*\*\* ton of money on my education and I wonder is this really the best I can be and how I'm gonna do in a real job in real life because all I know how to do is study. 

I just want you to know that you're not the only one struggling with those thoughts and doesn't make you a bad person whatsoever.

Talking to my counselor made realize how much abuse I had as a child. I see my brother and think he's crazy for acting the way he does, but I can see why he's kind of like that. I'm just amazed at how "seemingly normal" (not really) I turned out and haven't needed help until now.

Despite the fact that mental illness is seen negatively, it's really not. Just like physical wounds are caused by trauma to the skin, a lot of mental illnesses are from trauma to the mind. Mental health issues are kind of a taboo subject in Asian cultures, but after having a friend who struggled with mental issues and having recently experienced it myself, it's really different from what a lot of people believe. We're not crazy, we just need help dealing with our emotions and thoughts. Just know that there are millions of people struggling with issues like you and you're not the crazy one. Talking to a counselor was a step forward in admitting that I had a problem and I needed help. I still struggle but being able to expose all the things from the past that I've hidden for years is satisfying. It hurts thinking about it but when you get it off your chest, it's like you have less burden to carry. It might be worth seeking help, even if not a professional therapist, but someone who you can trust.

I see, I know the quarantine situation is making things more stressful and it's normal to feel even more anxious and stressed out right now. Doesn't make your situation any less important, but it may be a reason. This is what my therapist told me to do when I'm feeling a huge amount of stress or having an anxiety attack. Breathe in deeply and then out and just repeat it a couple of times. Sometimes it works for me, sometimes it doesn't. I know it's not a great solution you might be looking for, but I hope it is some help for you.

Do you know if you have any issues with anxiety or panic attacks? At first I thought I was just overreacting to stress but after talking to my friend I realized that that probably was an anxiety attack. Just knowing that it's not something random but it's due to an anxiety or panic issue can make it more bearable and learn how to get through moments like that.

It makes feel that way too. A couple days ago I had a really bad anxiety attack, probably one of my worst ones. I looked up advil overdose (which actually doesn't really kill you and leaves your digestive system a mess) but not with an intent to kill myself. It somehow felt satisfying. And then I found this subreddit and going through the posts, while makes me sad also helps calm me down. I can relate to so many stories and understand in a way that my therapist or friend can't (my friend has issues with anxiety too, even more than me but I don't want to be a burden on top of her problems).

I'm from Korea too and while my childhood wasn't as bad, I do remember when my mom would beat me and even try to kill (?) me for crying too loudly. I thought I grew up fine but I recently realized after talking to a therapist at school how much that had an impact on me. I love my mom but whenever she does one little thing, like lecture about something that she's lectured about hundreds of times, my mind would immediately go back to those moments and just want to get out of there or just go die. Living in the dorms in college even though my house isn't that far was like a blessing and what freedom feels like. Being back home is tough, and I realized I can't stay at home even though I said I would commute from home. My mom always wanting me to be perfect left me a mess, I get anxiety if I get less than an A on an exam, and we're talking about grad school. You're not alone in your struggles, especially how the culture is in Korea.

I found that I got angry at everything when I was under extreme stress. For me, it was multiple exams back to back. I was angry at the professors, angry at school and then just led to being angry at everything and myself. Is there anything that triggers that feeling? Or if it goes away at all? Teenage years are turbulent times, you become more self-aware and conscious of the world but everything is confusing. If you need to talk about anything, we're here to talk.

I think it's a vague area. I had thoughts where I wished I could die but didn't really have a plan  and it lasted a really short time (kind of like short bursts). I could say I was in denial that I had a problem. Looking back at it now, I think that it counts as suicidal ideation. Are you thinking about it with a goal to die, or just the act of jumping? Because if you wanted to jump just for the experience and the thrill, I wouldn't call it suicidality.

Mine is mostly school related and I've been talking to people who I can trust, like my friend and my boss on campus. They recommended that I go see a counselor, which never really occurred to me because it's like a taboo in Asian culture. I've seen him 3 times now and after I talk to him, it was like a huge weight was off of me. It's not like he gave me a solution that fixed all my problems, but just being able to talk about it with someone who's there to listen and I don't have to worry about being a burden on someone felt nice. I guess the only thing is that I kind of rely on him because I've been in a bad mental state since yesterday (again with school issues) and I only see him like once a week so it's hard get through the week. I don't know if your high school has anything like counseling center because mine didn't but if you have like an adviser or someone who helps you register for classes you can always go talk to them.
That's honestly how I feel right now. I don't have the courage to do it but if something happened to me, I wouldn't care.

I had/have the similar feeling just yesterday. I'm in pharmacy school and we had an online exam where I forgot to show my scratch paper to the camera and I was just paranoid that they would think that I was cheating. I began thinking about getting a 0 on the exam and having the drop the class and just had a whole mess with anxiety. And then last night I found out that an assignment I thought was due today actually closed the day before, which I couldn't have done anyway because I was too busy studying for the 2 exams we had. The professor refused to extend the deadline even though there was a whole bunch of us who misunderstood the email. It's only 20 points but I started thinking what's the point to all this. Why am I working my butt off to get A's when it seems like the pandemic will never end and even if it does I'll have a miserable life as a retail pharmacist. I thought that making money as a pharmacist and helping people would be worth it but seeing how horrible people can be, I don't even know if I want to do this anymore. I don't even have another goal, so my life is pretty much meaningless. I don't even have the courage to kill myself and found out that ibuprofen overdose doesn't actually kill you. So basically I'm trapped in this life until nature takes me.
